name: Dutch Republic (States General)

areaKm2.note: world_1650 Dutch Republic polygon = 32,996 km2 on the sphere. High allows for Generality Lands possibly drawn outside it.

population.note: HYDE via OWID: Netherlands 1,543,183 (1600) and 2,000,000 (1700); interpolated ~1.85M for 1672. The Military Revolution article gives 1.5M for c. 1650 and the Dutch States Army article "about 1.5 million in the 17th century". Generality Lands (Staats-Brabant, Staats-Vlaanderen, Maastricht) included.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Netherlands 22.0% (1600), 33.6% (1700) (de Vries, towns 10,000+); with the 5,000+ convention Holland exceeded 45%. Mid 38%: the most urbanised state in Europe.

activePersonnel.note: States Army establishment for 1672: 90,000 (Dutch States Army article, strength table), raised in haste from a peacetime ~30,000-40,000; the Franco-Dutch War article gives 80,000 and notes that contracts to exceed 80,000 took months to fill. Effective field army in June 1672 was far smaller (~22,000 under William III at the IJssel). Plus navy ~25,000 (28,000 personnel in 1670, Dutch States Navy table). Mid 76,000 = ~50,000 effective soldiers + ~26,000 navy.

trainedReserves.note: Schutterij civic militia: the cities provided 12,000 men in 1672 (Franco-Dutch War article); 50,000 militia backed 70,000 regulars in 1629 (Dutch States Army article).

supportPersonnel.note: Navy personnel 28,000 in 1670 (Dutch States Navy table after Rodger, Glete and others) incl. marines (Regiment de Marine, 1665), plus artillery and engineers (~1,500).

mobilizationRatio.note: Includes the mercenary market: the Republic hired Germans, Scots, English and Swiss (Dutch States Army article: without the open market for soldiers 1.5M people could not have competed). 90,000 army + 28,000 navy = ~6% of population in 1672-73; ceiling ~9-12% with foreign recruitment.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry companies of the States Army, much of it in fortress garrisons; strongly expanded with raw recruits in 1672 (Dutch States Army article). Effective count, not the 90,000 paper.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: matchlock and early flintlock muskets with pikes; Liege and Amsterdam arms industry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: the army had decayed during the stadholderless period; many 1672 recruits untrained; garrisons surrendered quickly

count.note: Cuirassier-type horse companies (~15% of the army).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: neglected before 1672

count.note: Educated guess: dragoons and light horse (dragoons counted as light cavalry).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: new units

count.note: Educated guess: field pieces; Dutch fortress artillery (thousands of guns) excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Dutch gun founding and Swedish iron guns among the best

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional gunners

count.note: Ships of the line: De Ruyter had 61 ships of the line (plus 14 frigates) at Solebay, 7 June 1672 (Battle of Solebay article, Blok 1928 and Van Nimwegen 2020); the Dutch States Navy table counts 110 warships of all classes in 1670.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: shallow-draught 60-80 gun ships, lighter than English first rates (Dutch States Navy article: 60-80 vs 70-100 guns)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: veteran crews of the Second Anglo-Dutch War (Medway 1667); De Ruyter the best admiral of the age

count.note: Frigates, fireships and yachts: 110 warships in 1670 (Dutch States Navy table) minus ships of the line; Solebay alone saw 14 frigates and ~24 fireships.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: good frigates

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: veteran crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: De Ruyter at sea the best of the era (0.95); on land William III untested in 1672 and the field army collapsed before the Water Line held; De Witt brothers murdered Aug 1672

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: mercenary regiments and provincial particularism (each province paid its own troops); navy cohesion high

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Rampjaar panic: towns surrendered without fighting, Orangist riots; recovered after Solebay and the inundations

weapons.note: Anchor: 5.3. Evidence: Maurician drill tradition, matchlock and pike, early flintlocks

ships.note: Anchor: 5.45. Evidence: two-deck ships of the line, line-of-battle tactics audit 2026-10-30: mid 5.45 -> 5.35, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1672 (5.351); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor: 5.4. Evidence: Old Dutch bastioned system and the Dutch Water Line inundations

logistics.note: Anchor: 5.6 above 5 (magazines, canal transport). Evidence: canal and river network, trekschuit services, the most advanced military contracting and credit system of the era audit 2026-10-30: mid 5.6 -> 5.35, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1672 (5.351); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

communications.note: Anchor: 5.4. Evidence: dense postal and newspaper network

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): Netherlands 1670 = 3,476, 1672 = 2,923 (the war-year collapse), 1680 = 3,549. Mid 3,200: the richest economy per head in the world.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: The Dutch States Army article (financing section) describes army and navy as the bulk of the Generality budget; Holland's debt service and war spending in 1672-73 reached ~8-12% of GDP (wartime mid, peacetime low ~4%).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: textiles (Leiden), shipbuilding (Zaan), sugar refining, brewing; services and trade large.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: the earliest fetched figure is Herrendorf et al. via OWID, Netherlands agriculture share of employment 1807 = 43.1% (1849 = 40.3%), https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/employment-by-economic-sector.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true. The Republic at its 1670s commercial peak was probably no more agrarian; a ~0.42 (0.35-0.50) assumed. No self-sufficiency figure fetched, so s = 1 is assumed, which overstates the value: Holland imported much of its bread grain from the Baltic (the moedernegotie) and its farms specialised in dairy. Grade D: a extrapolated over 135 years. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.05/0.1/0.15 (read as import dependence); recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: few roads; ~650 km of trekvaart canals plus rivers carried passengers and freight.

majorPorts.note: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Hellevoetsluis, Middelburg, Flushing, Enkhuizen, Hoorn, Harlingen, Den Helder.

merchantTonnage.note: Merchant fleet ~400,000-600,000 tons burden c. 1670, the largest in Europe (estimates after Vogel and de Vries/van der Woude summarised in the Dutch Republic literature); converted roughly to deadweight. Grade C.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Defensive war on interior water lines. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses for 1.85M people; transport mostly by boat.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row plus inundation: fortified cities and the Water Line (flooding stopped the French in June 1672); rated 1.3 for the water defence rather than climate.

notes: Snapshot = June 1672, the Rampjaar (French, Munster and Cologne invasion; Anglo-French naval attack; Solebay 7 June). Population: the Seven Provinces plus Generality Lands; VOC/WIC colonies are bases only (VOC troops excluded). Personnel convention: States Army regiments (largely foreign mercenaries) and navy are active; schutterij civic militia is trainedReserves. The 90,000 army figure is the 1672 establishment, not effectives; the effective field army in June was ~22,000-25,000 plus garrisons. Merchant tonnage is a conversion from tons burden, grade C.
